objective: Translate the owner-approved standalone Windows desktop decision and the submitted Park application requirements into a bounded first-release UX brief, proposed desktop-shell ADR, acceptance contract, and multidisciplinary review without changing executable behavior or scientific baselines.
previous_knowledge_consumed: Park application form AP-02-140503 defines a six-month four-phase R&D plan; unimplemented and unvalidated items remain objectives, not verified capabilities.
Main revision e30cc80b7a03f0c03e5fccbf6e339f0eb629e54c contains a FastAPI application and static Workbench but no verified Windows desktop shell or installer.
The current API entrypoint binds to 127.0.0.1:8000; a desktop shell requires managed service lifecycle and collision-safe port allocation.
DR24 raw inspection is separate from ALeRCE-normalized observations. HMJD, raw photometry, catflags, OID and filter identity must remain explicit.
The frozen v0.2.0 model artifact and DR24 feature parity remain unauthenticated/unapproved for DR24 inference.
Issue #293 requires written evaluation/demo licensing before external binary distribution.
The owner selected standalone Windows desktop delivery and approved parallel UI/UX work on 2026-11-24.

baseline.description: Documentation and architecture review against main. No code, data, model, feature schema, benchmark, release, or production configuration was changed.

correctness.reason: This cycle defines requirements and acceptance gates. No desktop executable or feature behavior was implemented.

reproducibility.reason: No Windows package or target-device run exists yet. Required build and evidence manifests are specified for a later cycle.

lifecycle_contract_coverage.reason: The documents define the required gates, but no executable desktop lifecycle has been tested.

knowledge_artifact_count.reason: Documentation artifacts were added, but no quantitative baseline metric was defined.

measurement.trade_off: Reuse the existing Workbench and FastAPI application behind a provisional Windows shell candidate. Defer selecting a GUI framework and adding dependencies until a bounded Windows proof-of-concept measures lifecycle, security, compatibility, and resource use.

evidence: Reviewed the submitted Park acceptance workbook AP-02-140503 and aligned the first-preview scope with its four-phase, six-month development plan.
Inspected main revision e30cc80b7a03f0c03e5fccbf6e339f0eb629e54c, including pyproject.toml, API entrypoint, API settings, FastAPI static Workbench mounting, DR24 routes, and observation service.
Verified that the current API entrypoint uses 127.0.0.1:8000 and that the package metadata does not define a desktop shell or Windows installer.
Added a UX brief, a provisional desktop-shell ADR, a simulated 16-role review, and a separate acceptance contract in PR #309.
The unique acceptance contract from duplicate PR #308 was copied to the canonical PR #309 branch; PR #308 was closed as superseded without merging.
The role-based review is explicitly a simulated AI-assisted review, not independent human peer review.
The proposed pywebview/WebView2 approach remains provisional. No desktop dependency was added.
No executable code, frozen baseline artifact, production data, scientific acceptance threshold, or release was changed.

Founder clarification on 2026-11-25 selects the Windows Laboratory Preview in this acceptance contract as the first delivery milestone; the Full six-month Park MVP remains inactive during the current scope freeze.

Founder clarification on 2026-11-25 supersedes the Persian/RTL UX requirement for this experimental preview. The Windows preview and installer are English-only; Persian localization may be considered for a later product release.

root_causes: The existing application is currently a local API with a browser-served Workbench, not a standalone Windows program.
The API entrypoint uses a fixed port and does not yet provide desktop-shell process lifecycle management.
The package metadata and workflows do not yet build or test a standalone Windows installer.
unresolved: The Windows shell framework has not passed a comparative proof-of-concept.
WebView2 runtime handling and clean-machine package behavior are not tested.
Local endpoint token/origin protections, navigation restrictions and port collision tests are not implemented.
Windows user-data paths, cache policy and installer upgrade/uninstall behavior are not tested.
A clean Windows 11 end-to-end DR24 workflow and user usability test remain unexecuted.
The written Park evaluation/demo license remains open.
Model artifact authentication, DR24 feature parity, AOIC identity and full Park cohort acceptance remain separate scientific blockers.

findings: A standalone Windows preview is a scope change from the earlier browser-only demonstrator plan and must have its own explicit acceptance contract.
The first useful user journey is DR24 retrieval, source-native inspection, diagnostic QC, descriptive summary, provenance and JSON export.
A browser UI displayed inside a desktop shell is not proof of a packaged, self-contained Windows application.
A successful Linux CI or browser contract test does not prove installation or operation on clean Windows.
The current fixed port and relative default data paths require explicit desktop runtime design.
The first preview and the full six-month Park MVP require separate readiness decisions.
Classification and discovery claims must remain blocked until model, feature, identity and validation gates pass.

open_blockers: Run a bounded Windows shell comparison and select the framework only after the proof-of-concept.
Implement and test managed local API startup, readiness, ephemeral port selection, loopback-only binding, request protection and shutdown.
Implement per-user workspace/cache/log paths and verify no protected installation-directory writes.
Build a Windows x64 package and test install, launch, live retrieval, export, upgrade and uninstall on a clean Windows 11 device.
Obtain written limited Park evaluation/demo terms and review third-party component licenses.
Keep original v0.2.0 model, DR24 feature parity, AOIC and CPVS validation gates separate and unchanged.

knowledge_carried_forward: PR #309 is the canonical documentation track for Windows desktop UX and architecture.
PR #308 is superseded and closed; its unique acceptance contract is retained in PR #309.
No desktop framework or new dependency is approved until the bounded technical spike passes.
The first Windows preview is limited to real DR24 exploration and descriptive analysis unless further scientific gates pass.
Preserve v0.2.0 and keep CPVS discrepancy separate.
No external installer release before clean Windows acceptance and written legal approval.
For the current Park delivery, implement only the Windows Laboratory Preview acceptance workflow and gates. Do not interpret the broader six-month dossier roadmap as work that must run in parallel.
